content:
iPadOS and macOS were originally two distinctly different software platforms. But since iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. This year it's even more apparent, with iPadOS 27 adding three features that bring the iPad closer to the Mac than ever before.

#1: Status bar shows app name

I usually use my M5 iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard attached at all times. The iPad has always had one issue: it lacks a clear "current app" indicator for keyboard users.

If there's only one app on screen, there's no problem. But if you have several apps open simultaneously, keyboard shortcuts become very difficult to manage. I can't count how many times I've thought a shortcut was triggered in one app, only to find it was executed in another.

Mac solved this problem a long time ago, displaying the name of the active app in the top-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 does this too.

iPadOS 27 users will find the name of the active app displayed alongside other status bar elements, such as the time and date. This may be a small change, but it's very practical, making keyboard operation of the iPad a more comfortable experience.

#2: Permanently visible menu bar

Another change in iPadOS 27 is the option to set the menu bar to always be displayed.

Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time last year. However, unlike the Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appears when the user actively summons it.

In the Settings app on iPadOS 27, under "Multitasking & Gestures", there's a new toggle option that reads: "Auto-show and hide menu bar".

After turning off this toggle, the menu bar will remain visible at all times. I've been using it for a while during the iPadOS beta period, and this is one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday operation speed on par with Mac

Although I really love my iPad and am grateful for the new features brought by iPadOS 26 and 27, I sometimes get frustrated because some basic operations are too slow. For instance, I wrote earlier this year: "Using right-click on iPadOS often feels slow and laggy, but on the Mac, it's an instant response."

Thanks to Apple's focus this year on fixing bugs, I'm happy to say that iPadOS 27 has improved in speed for these kinds of everyday operations.

Apple says right-click menus open faster when using a mouse, and I can definitely feel it. Browsing files and transferring files to external drives is "up to 5 times faster", which Apple says now matches Finder on the Mac. App launch responsiveness is snappier, and window management for closing, switching, or dragging windows is also faster.

There are still some areas where the Mac is faster than the iPad, and the iPad can still feel slow at times. Overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a big step in the right direction.

What are your favourite new features and changes in iPadOS 27? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
